todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Sep 29 that Qatar was exchanging US-Iran messages. Trump denied offering sanctions relief or frozen funds; talks had not produced a Hormuz reopening agreement.

Reuters reported Sep 29 that Saudi Arabia resumed Yanbu tanker loadings after restarting the East-West Pipeline. Revised Sep 28 Kpler estimates put regional exports at 16.328 million bpd and Hormuz exports at 9.719 million bpd.

The latest reviewed Reuters/Kpler daily count remains nine commodity vessels on Sep 24, versus an 18-vessel 10-day average. No current LNG-specific transit count or route-normalised LNG freight observation was approved.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Qatar is mediating, but a signed, monitored reopening and verified shipping normalisation are still required. Trump denied offering sanctions relief; no Hormuz reopening agreement is verified.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Selective Hormuz transits persist while Saudi Arabia resumes Yanbu loadings after restarting its East-West Pipeline. Revised September export estimates show recovery, but LNG transit and replacement supply data remain incomplete.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Negotiations fail or verified attacks disrupt Hormuz and alternative export routes. Iran retains its approved-route and fee conditions; current replacement LNG, route-normalised freight and cargo-normalised war-risk costs remain unverified.
